description: Pinned external tools used by this project. Neither yt-dlp nor ffmpeg is downloaded as a prebuilt binary: both are built from their pinned git submodule source (vendor/yt-dlp, vendor/ffmpeg) by build-ytdlp.bat and build-ffmpeg.bat respectively. This file records the toolchain download-dependencies.bat bootstraps to make those builds possible, plus provenance notes for the toolchain packages that are pinnable.

ffmpeg.note: No longer a downloaded binary. ffmpeg.exe and ffprobe.exe are built from vendor/ffmpeg (git submodule of https://github.com/FFmpeg/FFmpeg) by build-ffmpeg.bat. See docs/features/build-and-packaging/building-ffmpeg-from-source.md for the exact configure flags, the LGPL licence decision, and verification evidence. The resulting binaries' provenance (submodule commit, version, SHA-256 of each binary, configure flags, licence, build timestamp) is recorded per-build in vendor/bin/ffmpeg.build.json rather than pinned here, because it is a build output, not a fetched artifact.

yt-dlp.note: Not a downloaded binary either. yt-dlp.exe is built from vendor/yt-dlp (git submodule) by build-ytdlp.bat. Its provenance is recorded per-build in vendor/bin/yt-dlp.build.json. See docs/features/build-and-packaging/building-yt-dlp-from-source.md.

python.note: fallbackInstallerSha256 is intentionally blank: it was never downloaded and verified during this task, so no digest is recorded rather than an invented one. download-dependencies.bat only reaches this fallback when winget is unavailable, and it refuses to run the fallback installer while this value is blank, reporting the exact blocker instead. Fill this in only after downloading the asset yourself and computing its real SHA-256.

msys2.purpose: Provides the mingw-w64 GCC toolchain, nasm, make, pkg-config and diffutils that ffmpeg's own ./configure and make need to produce a native Windows ffmpeg.exe/ffprobe.exe, plus the LGPL-compatible codec libraries build-ffmpeg.bat enables (gnutls, zlib, mp3lame, opus, vorbis). No GPL-only library (libx264, libvpx) is installed, because build-ffmpeg.bat never enables one -- see docs/features/build-and-packaging/building-ffmpeg-from-source.md. Bootstrapped by download-dependencies.bat, consumed by build-ffmpeg.bat. GitHub's windows-latest Actions runner image already ships MSYS2 at C:\msys64, so the release workflow reuses it instead of installing a second copy.
msys2.note: These are rolling-release pacman packages; MSYS2 does not publish stable per-package version pins the way a fixed-release ecosystem does, so no version number or digest is recorded here beyond the package name list itself. The reproducibility guarantee in this project comes from the pinned ffmpeg submodule commit (vendor/ffmpeg) and the recorded configure flags, not from pinning the compiler's own version.
